moat_against: Single-customer concentration: substantially all backlog is U.S. government orders
Government sets the economics: cost-plus / fixed-price-incentive contracts cap upside and leave overruns with HII
No commercial pricing power; labor shortages and throughput delays hit margins directly
ROIC proxy compressed to 6.5–10.2% (FY2021–FY2025) from 21–32% (FY2016–FY2020); operating margin 4.6–6.8% recently
Mission Technologies competes in contested defense-services markets
moat_for: Sole-source nuclear aircraft carrier design, build and refueling (Newport News); Truman RCOH awarded without competition
One of only two U.S. nuclear-submarine builders (Virginia/Columbia class with General Dynamics)
Absolute barriers: nuclear certification, dry docks, cleared skilled workforce, decades of Navy integration
$57.3B backlog at 2026-06-30; each carrier built creates a ~50-year sole-source refueling/overhaul tail
moat_justification: Sole U.S. designer/builder/refueler of nuclear-powered aircraft carriers and one of only two nuclear-submarine builders, with a $57.3B backlog — an effectively unbreachable franchise position. But the U.S. government is a monopsonist customer that caps margins by contract structure, and measured returns have compressed: fundamentals.json roic_proxy fell from 21–32% in FY2016–FY2020 to 6.5–10.2% in FY2021–FY2025, with operating margin at 4.6–6.8% over the same recent period. Durable franchise, contract-capped economics — 6, not 7+.
name: Huntington Ingalls Industries, Inc.
one_liner: Irreplaceable sole-source nuclear shipbuilder, moat 6/10, but contract-capped margins and violently lumpy cash conversion — at $270 it does not clear 15% (weighted IRR 10.33%, IV@15 $163.99); it would clear 15% only at or below ~$164.
